references.text: Aroer by the Arnon River is mentioned again as the boundary of the land taken from Sihon and given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
Aroer on the bank of the Arnon River is described as the southern border of the conquered land.
Joshua describes the kingdom of Sihon as extending from Aroer by the Arnon River, confirming the conquest mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Aroer by the Arnon River is noted as part of the inheritance given to the tribe of Reuben.
The boundary of Reuben's inheritance is described starting from Aroer by the Arnon River.
Jephthah refers to Israel's settlement in Aroer and the areas along the Arnon as proof of their rightful ownership.
Israel defeated Sihon and took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, the original account of the conquest.
Aroer is mentioned among the cities rebuilt by the children of Gad in the conquered land.
